source.title_on_document: Dialogue patterns in human-AI co-creation: how interaction structure shapes output and process

supplement.where: No supplementary material or online appendix is mentioned. Appendices A (system prompts), B (dialogue-act scheme), and C (coding validation) are inside this PDF, PDF pp. 30-32.
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the main text. Data are 'available from the corresponding author on reasonable request' (PDF p. 27, Data availability statement).

paper_design_summary: 275 US MTurk workers were randomly assigned to one of four AI interaction designs, all using the same model (Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite): human-lead expand, AI-lead propose, iterative critique, and free dialogue. Each wrote a user persona and scenario for a seed-trading gardening app; 244 remained after exclusions. Three blinded raters scored originality and appropriateness (summed into a composite creativity score); the paper also measures descriptive richness (adjective and adverb share) and between-persona embedding similarity within each condition against a permutation null. There is no no-AI arm.

studies.label: Four-condition between-subjects experiment on human-AI interaction patterns (persona creation task)

assignment.what_was_assigned: One of four human-AI interaction designs (HLE, ALP, IC, FD); all four use the same generative AI model with different interfaces and system prompts
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one condition and completed a user persona creation task with AI assistance structured according to their assigned pattern.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 8), Section 4.1; sequential balancing described in the same section
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 8), Section 4.2: 'Substantial exclusions were applied based on pre-registered quality criteria'. PDF p. 22, Section 5.6 mentions an interpretive rule for kappa 'we set in advance'. No registry name, ID, or link is given, and the paper does not say which outcomes were preregistered.

arms.name: Human-lead expand (HLE)
arms.description: Participant drafts; a dropdown menu triggers AI expansions (demographics, scenario ideas, goals, frustrations, personality) shown in a separate panel that the participant must integrate by hand.

arms.name: AI-lead propose (ALP)
arms.description: AI first shows five persona concepts; participant picks one and develops it, with the AI available in chat but restricted to elaborating the chosen concept.

arms.name: Iterative critique (IC)
arms.description: Participant drafts alone and clicks 'Get Feedback' for structured AI critique (strengths, areas for improvement, recommendations); the AI does not produce drafts.

arms.name: Free dialogue (FD)
arms.description: Unconstrained chat with the AI in a split pane beside the workspace; the AI can see but not edit the workspace. System prompt asks it to be constructively critical.

participants.exclusions: 31 of 275 assigned participants excluded under pre-registered quality criteria: repeat participation (MTurk ID or IP), fewer than 3 logged interactions or under 3 minutes, and RA-flagged bot-like, nonsensical, or inattentive submissions. Per-arm counts at assignment and per-arm exclusions are not reported; per-arm analyzed counts (60/62/61/61) are in Table 1 and Figure 2.
participants.who: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers in the US with HIT approval rate of 99 percent or higher and at least 1000 prior HITs; $2 base pay plus $10-$30 bonuses for top-rated submissions
participants.quote: A total of 275 participants were initially assigned to one of four human–AI interaction patterns. After applying the predefined data quality criteria, 31 participants were excluded, resulting in a final sample of 244 participants.
participants.locator: PDF pp. 9-10 (journal pp. 8-9), Section 4.2; Table 1 and Figure 2 on PDF p. 10 (journal p. 9)

ai_tool.name_model: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite (preview release 09/2025), via OpenRouter as google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-09-2025, condition-specific system prompts (Appendix A)
ai_tool.how_used: Role differs by arm: HLE = on-demand content expansions from a menu (close to suggestions); ALP = AI supplies five persona concepts then limited elaboration chat (ideas_supplied); IC = structured critique of the participant's draft (refinement); FD = open chat with a critical-collaborator prompt (open_chat). In every arm the participant writes the final artifact by hand; the AI cannot edit the workspace.

task.description: Co-create a user persona (name, demographics) and a usage scenario for a hypothetical mobile app that helps local gardeners trade seeds and produce.
task.duration: Advertised as about 20-40 min; mean task duration 10:13 (min:sec), by arm 9:13 (HLE), 9:08 (ALP), 10:36 (IC), 11:59 (FD) (Table 1).

outcomes.name: Composite creativity score (originality + appropriateness, 0-20)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Sum of originality and appropriateness (each 10-point), each averaged over three independent blinded external judges 'with backgrounds relevant to evaluating narrative artifacts (e.g., creative writing)'. ICC(3,3) = .84, 95% CI [.80, .87]. Convergent check with Qwen3-32B ratings (rs = .71 for overall creativity), not reported by condition. Omnibus Brown-Forsythe test used because Levene's test rejected equal variances.

outcomes.name: Descriptive richness (share of adjectives and adverbs in the text)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: DR = (n_adj + n_adv) / n_tokens, tokens excluding punctuation; a part-of-speech count, not a creativity scoring model. The paper treats it as a proxy for elaboration, not writing quality, and notes it was not validated against human judgments. Kruskal-Wallis omnibus, Dunn post hoc with Holm correction.

outcomes.name: Between-persona semantic similarity within condition (homogenization)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity for every pair of personas, computed separately for persona content, scenario content, and combined text, with two embedding models (6 model-by-content cells). Robustness: length-controlled version that projects out the length-correlated embedding direction gives the same direction with larger z scores; uncontrolled values are primary.

diversity_detail.metric: Within-condition mean pairwise cosine similarity, compared with a permutation null; framed as semantic distance (1 minus cosine) following Anderson et al. (2024)
diversity_detail.embedding_model: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 and jina-embeddings-v2-base-en (8,192-token context; no persona truncated, max 2,235 tokens)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of personas within a condition (persona content, scenario content, and combined text separately); baseline is the between-condition mean pairwise similarity
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Permutation test shuffling condition labels 10,000 times; two-sided p with Holm-Bonferroni correction across four conditions; z scores reported
diversity_detail.notes: No direct arm-versus-arm test of diversity is reported; each arm is compared with the permutation null. Per-arm similarity levels are printed only for the surviving cells (IC persona, ALP combined); the rest appear as violin plots in Figure 6.

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned to one of four generative-AI configurations (no no-AI arm), which fits the ai_design comparison. 244 people analyzed (275 assigned), 60-62 per arm. Rated creativity, originality, and appropriateness, plus embedding-based similarity, are scored on the persona each participant wrote. All contrasts are AI configuration versus AI configuration; none is AI versus no AI.

one_line_finding: Among 244 MTurk workers using one of four AI interaction designs, iterative critique scored higher than AI-lead propose on composite creativity (17.57 vs 15.92 of 20; difference 1.64, 95% CI [.096, 3.191], p = .033; Section 5.1.2, PDF p. 16), originality did not differ (F(3, 240) = 2.42, p = .084), and iterative-critique personas were more alike than chance (z = +2.59 and +2.79; Section 5.5, PDF p. 21).
open_questions: Which arm is the control for ai_design contrasts? No arm is plain or default. I used free dialogue (closest to free chatbot use) as the control and also recorded IC vs ALP, the paper's only Holm-surviving creativity contrast.
Rater type: the three judges have 'backgrounds relevant to evaluating narrative artifacts (e.g., creative writing)'. I coded expert_raters; a reviewer may prefer human_raters.
Descriptive richness (adjective plus adverb share) is coded as elaboration with measure automated_score; it is a part-of-speech count, not a creativity model.
Diversity outcome compares each arm with a permutation null, not arm with arm, so it does not map directly onto the codebook's arm-difference contrast.
Per-arm counts at assignment are not reported (only 275 in total), so n_randomized per arm is null.
Preregistration is mentioned only for exclusion criteria; no registry ID and no statement that the composite creativity score was a preregistered primary outcome.
notes: PDF page numbers are journal page + 1 because of the publisher cover page. Not listed as outcomes: Qwen3-32B LLM ratings (used only as a validity check, rs = .77/.78/.71 with human composites, not by condition; PDF p. 15); vocabulary diversity (only a correlation with message length, rs = -0.147; PDF p. 24); DAT baseline creativity (measured before the task); self-reported mental demand, trust, control, AI role, and ownership (self-report, excluded by criterion 3); process measures (entropy, interaction count). The paper's Figure 7 d values use pooled SD, 10,000-resample bootstrap CIs, and Welch t-tests with Holm correction per outcome; only the d values are printed, not the CIs. The originality ANOVA F(3, 240) = 2.42 is printed with p = .084; I recorded it as printed.
